analysis: The supplied changes are documentation only. The patch to docs/reference/configuration.md (head lines 618-625, in the Model verification I/O section) and the patch to docs/reference/model-registry-format.md (head lines 120-122, plus the date bump at line 3) describe an overlapped uncached hashing reader. It uses a reader thread one 4 MiB chunk ahead of SHA-256, with two page-aligned buffers per file. The text states that the verified bytes, the full SHA, the sorted-key combination and the existing fallbacks are unchanged. No source code, wire contract, key handling, attestation path, authorization path or cache encryption path changed in the supplied evidence. The mode-only or metadata-only unit 8a0bb3b7597b92da:0 carries no content and no security-relevant change. The head_text excerpt of configuration.md (lines 491-757) is surrounding context and contains only unchanged configuration documentation. I did not verify that it shows no security-relevant drift, such as the prefix-cache TTL, the SSD cache variables relevant to T-041, or the environment scrubber list. Relevant threat areas for context are T-012/T-027 (weight integrity and substitution) and A-004. The documented behavior says hash verification still covers the full file contents, so no regression is visible. Open question for later passes: the actual implementation (WeightHasher.swift and OverlappedFileDigest.swift) was not supplied, so the claims that a failed read or worker error prevents a successful aggregate hash, and that buffers and pages are dropped correctly, remain unverified. Only the documentation's assertions were reviewed. The doc claim that the 'Any failed file prevents a successful aggregate' behavior still holds is carried from the unchanged text at head line 636.
